content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge is resolving a link by matching [CR2] G against the challenger's rows, so K-C's chain-vs-chain method governs the grading.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'leaving the sign's sense open' could mean (1) the defender's chain does not resolve the sign, a permissible underdetermination, or (2) a demand that a verse or chain expressly state the sign's sense, which would be the retired stating-verse test; I weigh it as (1) because the text does not mention a contrary statement.","why":"The judge's reason is a chain-level underdetermination after G answers the rows, not a verse-by-verse demand that some verse state the contrary, so it does not breach K-C."}
